murrayville-guide.name: Murrayville
murrayville-guide.summary: Murrayville is the established family neighbourhood on the hill just east of Langley City, with tree-lined streets, sidewalks, Langley Memorial Hospital and the W.C. Blair Recreation Centre, and farmland starting right at its edge.
murrayville-guide.verdict: Pick Murrayville for a quiet, established family street. Look elsewhere if you need a suite to help with the mortgage.
murrayville-guide.vibe: Established and leafy: sidewalks, big trees and family streets, with farm country starting at the edge.

commute.from: Murrayville (OpenStreetMap place point, near 48 Avenue and 216 Street)

works.t: Tree-lined streets with sidewalks, much like Walnut Grove.
Fewer cars parked on the street, because fewer houses have suites.
W.C. Blair Recreation Centre (wave pool, six 25 m lanes, climbing wall) and McLeod Athletic Park (track, lighted turf fields, tennis and pickleball) are in the neighbourhood.
Langley Memorial Hospital, with 24/7 emergency care, is at 22051 Fraser Highway.
Groceries close by: the IGA at 22259 48 Avenue and Ralph’s, plus Shoppers Drug Mart in Murrayville Square.
Bigger lots than the newer suburbs: the typical house that sold sat on about 7,500 square feet.

doesnt.t: Not many houses have a mortgage-helper suite.
Highway 1 is about 12 minutes away off-peak, via 216 Street and Glover Road, farther than from Walnut Grove or Willoughby.
No SkyTrain. The bus to Langley Centre is route 560, and the Langley City SkyTrain extension is expected to open in late 2029.
The hospital’s emergency department and Langley Regional Airport (5385 216 Street) are here. If you’re sensitive to sirens or aircraft, visit the street at a few different times.
Near Murray’s Corner, the heritage conservation area means exterior changes, demolition or subdivision can need a heritage permit.

fit.q: Do you need a basement suite to help pay the mortgage?
fit.a: Then Murrayville makes it harder. Few houses have one. Walnut Grove and Willoughby have more.

fit.q: Do you drive to Surrey or Vancouver most days?
fit.a: Allow about 12 minutes to reach Highway 1 off-peak, 30 minutes to Surrey Central and 54 minutes to downtown Vancouver, before traffic.

fit.q: Would you rather have an established street than a brand-new subdivision?
fit.a: That’s Murrayville’s strength: mature trees, sidewalks and bigger lots. The typical house that sold here was built in 1993.

fit.q: Is a pool, a rec centre and a hospital close by on your list?
fit.a: W.C. Blair, McLeod Athletic Park and Langley Memorial Hospital are all inside the neighbourhood.

faq.q: Is Murrayville a good place to live?
faq.a: For families who want an established street, yes. Murrayville has tree-lined streets with sidewalks, bigger lots, the W.C. Blair Recreation Centre and Langley Memorial Hospital. The trade-offs are few houses with suites and a longer drive to Highway 1 than Walnut Grove or Willoughby.

faq.q: What are the downsides of living in Murrayville?
faq.a: Few houses have a mortgage-helper suite, Highway 1 is about 12 minutes away off-peak, there is no SkyTrain yet, and homes near the hospital or Langley Regional Airport can hear sirens or aircraft. Exterior changes in the heritage area near Murray’s Corner can need a permit.
